chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Sinānī and ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Mūsā al-Daqqāq narrated, saying: Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā al-Qaṭṭān narrated to us. He said: Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥabīb narrated to us. He said: Tamīm ibn Buhlūl narrated to us, from his father, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-ʿAbdī, from Sulaymān ibn Mihrān, who said:

I said to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, “How many times did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله perform hajj?” He said, “Twenty pilgrimages, concealed; in every pilgrimage he would pass by al-Maʾzimayn, then dismount and urinate.”

I said to him, “O son of the Messenger of Allah, why would he dismount there and urinate?” He said, “Because it was a place in which idols had been worshipped, and from it was taken the stone from which Hubal was carved, the one that ʿAlī عليه السلام threw from the top of the Kaʿbah when he climbed upon the back of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. Then he ordered concerning it, so it was buried near the gate of Banī Shaybah. Thus entering the mosque from the gate of Banī Shaybah became a sunnah because of that.”

Sulaymān said: I said, “Then how is it that the takbīr removes the constriction there?” He said, “Because the servant’s saying, ‘Allāhu Akbar,’ means that Allah is greater than being like the carved idols and the deities worshipped besides Him. And indeed Iblīs among his devils constricts the pilgrims’ passage in that place; so when he hears the takbīr, he flies off with his devils, and the angels follow them until they fall into the green abyss.”

I said, “How is it that it is recommended for the first-time pilgrim to enter the Kaʿbah rather than one who has already performed hajj?” He said, “Because the first-time pilgrim is fulfilling an obligation, invited to the pilgrimage of the House of Allah; so it is fitting that he enter the House to which he was invited, so that he may be honored within it.”

I said, “How is shaving made obligatory for him rather than for one who has already performed hajj?” He said, “So that by that he may be marked with the mark of the secure ones. Do you not hear the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who says: ‘You shall surely enter al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, if Allah wills, secure, with your heads shaved and shortened, not fearing’?”
I said, “Then how did stepping upon al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām become an obligation upon him?” He said, “So that by that he may deserve stepping into the spacious center of Paradise.”

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: the declaration 'Allāhu Akbar,' described here as repelling constriction and devils
key_terms.الصَّرُورَةُ: the first-time pilgrim who is fulfilling the obligatory hajj
key_terms.الْأَصْنَامُ: idols, referenced as objects formerly worshipped at that location
key_terms.الْحَلْقُ: shaving the head as a hajj rite, here described as obligatory for the first-time pilgrim
key_terms.الْمَأْزِمَيْنِ: the narrow pass mentioned as a place the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would pass during hajj
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ: the sacred site whose treading is described as an obligation in the pilgrimage
key_terms.بُحْبُوحَةِ الْجَنَّةِ: the spacious middle of Paradise, mentioned as a reward

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the wisdom behind certain rites of hajj and the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم pilgrimages?
ai.summary: This hadith relates several merits and reasons connected to hajj rites, including the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم pilgrimages, the significance of al-Maʾzimayn, takbīr, entering the Kaʿbah, shaving the head, and al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām. It ties these rites to the rejection of idolatry, honoring the invited pilgrim, Qur’anic language about safety and shaving, and the hope of reward in Paradise.
